images.title: An altitude of a triangle
images.purpose: Show the altitude as the perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side.
images.composition: One acute triangle with its base horizontal and the single altitude drawn from the top vertex, centred with lots of white space.
exact_structure: Triangle ABC, all angles acute, base BC horizontal at the bottom, B left, C right, A above, with the foot D on BC between B and C.
Sides in teal (#0072B2) outline with a light fill.
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) solid segment AD from A straight down to D on BC.
A small square right-angle mark at D, labelled 90°. The segment AD carries the word altitude beside it.
A thin grey (#6B7280) double-headed arrow beside AD marking its length, labelled height.
rejection: AD drawn slanted instead of at 90° to BC
the foot D outside segment BC
images.takeaway: The altitude is the perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side, and its length is the height.
images.description: Triangle ABC with the perpendicular AD from A to BC and a right angle at D.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Trace AD with a finger and check that it meets the base at a square corner.

image_decisions.why: The perpendicular from the vertex is the whole definition of an altitude.
